Thanks Hannah. I pulled the attached PDF and reviewed it quickly. Checklist for acceptance:
- Purchaser name exactly matching billing account: REQUIRED
- Certificate form must be signed and dated: PREFERRED (unsigned can sometimes be accepted with additional corroboration)
- States covered listed explicitly: REQUIRED
- Blanket/transaction-specific indicator: OK either way but we need to record which it is
- Purchasers tax ID/EIN: HELPFUL (not always required)

The June file has purchaser name and states, but its missing a signature block and theres no EIN. Before we mark INV-2026-0921 exempt, well either need a signed copy or an affirmation from Brightline that the attached is their official certificate plus a statement confirming their EIN.

Ill hold the invoice in our system pending receipt. Erin, could you provide either a signed/dated PDF or confirmation of the EIN for Brightline? If you can upload to DocuSign or send as the signed PDF, that will speed things.

Subject: RE: Resale certificate and nexus question for Redwood invoices

Quick nexus note: I ran Brightlines shipping and billing addresses (CA, OR, and NY are the primary states listed) against Redwoods presence. Short summary:
- CA: Redwood has remote sales presence (support contractors) and model serving endpoints in us-west that may establish economic nexus depending on revenue thresholds. Need to confirm Brightlines taxable product classification for CA.
- OR: no sales tax in OR; certificate coverage is fine.
- NY: no physical presence for Redwood, but we do hit economic thresholds for certain SaaS transactions in NY. I recommend we treat NY as potentially taxable until we confirm the certificate covers software services sold to Brightline.

Action items for Brightline: please confirm the certificate is intended to cover "software as a service / digital subscriptions" and send the EIN or a signed copy. If theyre able to sign the form and upload to DocuSign, that will let us clear CA and NY faster.

- Rishi
Tax Compliance Analyst
